chunks: And from him, from Abd al-Rahman, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from 'Isa ibn al-Qasim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the purchase of camels to be taken out from Mecca and Medina, so he said: 'I do not like that anything be taken out from them.'
And if the person in ihram brings a bird into the Sanctuary, it is not for him to take it out from it, and if he takes it out, then upon him is the blood offering (dam). Narrated.

key_terms.الْحَرَمَ: The Sanctuary (specifically the Haram of Mecca or Medina)
key_terms.الْقَمَارِيِّ: Camels (plural of qamarah, often used for camels brought for trade or sacrifice)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in ihram (state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.دَمٌ: Blood offering (a specific type of compensation in Hajj jurisprudence)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling and compensation for bringing a bird into the Haram while in ihram and then taking it out?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the status of livestock and birds within the sanctuaries, expressing a preference that they not be removed from Mecca and Medina. The hadith establishes a specific legal precedent for the *dam* (blood offering) penalty when a person in *ihram* intentionally brings a bird into the Haram and subsequently removes it, highlighting the sanctity of the space even during the state of pilgrimage. This ruling underscores the intersection of commercial activity and ritual purity within the holy boundaries.
